name: @khorsheed/dsh-reader
description: Link reader tab: RSS/Atom subscriptions plus pasted article links, a card feed with a readable detail view, host-side fetch and daily refresh over a Typert Remote data face

compat.notes: A page-type right-Sidebar tab (minted kind `reader`) over a Typert Remote data face. Fetching runs on the HOST through the sanctioned `ctx.web` seam; state is written with plain `node:fs` (atomic temp+rename) under `$DSH_HOME/state/dsh-reader`, NOT through `ctx.fs` — that service is the session-fenced sandboxed filesystem, so a workspace-write session refuses a write to the state root (observed on the acceptance instance). Every optional capability is probed at apply time and degrades (no `web` → domain refusals; no `sideChat` → the side-chat gesture hides; no `quote` → selection quoting is unavailable while the entry-level quote button still works). KNOWN LIMIT: the host fetch seam caps a decoded body at 100,000 chars and truncates silently, so articles larger than that cannot be extracted — the detail view falls back to a 「受限篇幅，内容未完整呈现」 notice with a 「阅读原文」 button (measured: Anthropic research pages, theverge.com, newyorker.com). On-device translation (0.2.0) runs the page's own Translator API (Chrome 138+/Edge 148+, desktop): the model never leaves the device and no model quota is spent, while the derived sentence pairs persist on the host (a global memory file plus per-entry segment maps under the state root, one shared budget, no TTL) so a reload re-paints instead of re-translating. Where that API is absent or the pair is unavailable, the globe is simply not rendered — the pane keeps working exactly as before. Source bodies that are already Chinese are not offered translation at all. On host 0.1.6-alpha.2+ the spots that want a real browser (the script-figure notice, a bot-wall card's action) open the in-app Sidebar Browser tab, probed through the `browser` tab kind; on older hosts they are the ordinary external link. Pages that inline real figures as base64 data URIs are now kept whole (substantive payloads over a 512-char threshold; 1px placeholders still yield to lazy-loading attributes), so a figure-heavy paper on a cap-raised deployment becomes a multi-MB cached body by design — bodies are bounded by entry count + TTL, not by a char budget.
